title: DR1's CPH page explains what a CPH number is and where to find one, behind a "What is a CPH number?" expander; the frontend page carries no help content at all.

finding.frontend: The page opens on the error summary and goes straight to the form and the single input (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/template.njk:6-25); the copy file holds a title, a label, a hint and three error messages, and no help strings (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/cph-number/copy/copy.en.js:1-12). fe-cph-number is a heading, an example and a box. A trader who does not know what a CPH number is, or does not know they have one, has nothing on the page to work from and no route to finding out.
finding.prototype: Between the heading and the input DR1 puts a govukDetails summarised "What is a CPH number?" holding two paragraphs: "A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled." and "You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.", with the last clause a link (app/views/cph-number.html:45-51). dr1-cph-number shows it collapsed, above the field, so it costs a trader who already knows nothing.
finding.difference: Add the expander with both paragraphs, above the input. The GOV.UK destination for the second paragraph is still open — DR1's own href is a placeholder — so either the real holding-details page has to be found or the second paragraph ships without the link, naming APHA documents only.
finding.falsifiedBy: Any help content about what a CPH number is appearing on the frontend page or in its copy file.

relatedTo.why: both are content on the same page — one the heading, the other the help block beneath it
